card.title: Graphical LPP — corners hold the optimum

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Linear programming optimises a linear objective (maximise profit, minimise cost) over a polygonal feasible region cut by linear constraints. The fundamental theorem: optima live at CORNERS — so graph the inequalities, shade feasibility, evaluate Z at each vertex, pick the extreme. Formulation (variables → objective → constraints → non-negativity) is half the marks.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: form: maximise Z = ax + by s.t. constraints + x,y ≥ 0  ·  method: graph lines → shade feasible polygon → list vertices → evaluate Z each → max/min wins  ·  iso-profit lines (parallel Z-slides) confirm visually

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Two variables only (graphical method's limit). Bounded feasible region guarantees a vertex optimum; unbounded needs an outward check (Z may run to infinity). Non-negativity (x, y ≥ 0) is a constraint, not optional decoration. Integer answers need integer programming (beyond syllabus — round with care).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Infeasible (empty region — contradictory constraints) and unbounded (infinite optimum) are valid answers, not errors. Multiple optima: a whole edge ties (objective parallel to a constraint). Degenerate vertices (3+ lines concurrent) still evaluate normally.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Maximise Z = 3x + 4y s.t. x + y ≤ 4, x, y ≥ 0 (+ one more constraint): vertices (0,0), (4,0), (0,4) [with extra constraint, list all] → Z values 0, 12, 16 → max 16 at (0,4). Corner evaluation beats all calculus here — linearity guarantees it.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Graphical method dies at three variables (simplex territory). Linearity is assumed — diminishing returns need nonlinear programming. Corner theorem needs convex polygonal regions (non-convex feasibility breaks the guarantee).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Why corners? Level sets of Z are parallel lines; sliding the line across a convex polygon, last contact must be a vertex (or full edge) — extreme of a linear function over a polytope always attained at extreme points. Formulation derives from accounting: decision variables × unit contributions = objective; resource caps = constraints.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Formulation first (Z + constraints + x,y ≥ 0) — half marks secured. Graph carefully (intercepts fastest). List ALL vertices (intersections pairwise). Evaluate Z at each — no calculus, no second-guessing.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: formulate an LPP from a word problem; graphical solution with feasible-region shading; max/min identification with vertex table; infeasible/unbounded verdicts.
